title: Device-Algorithm Co-Design of Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory In-Situ Annealer for Combinatorial Optimization Problems
problem: Combinatorial optimization problems require O(n²) vector-matrix-vector multiplications for Ising energy computation and complex exponential annealing factors, making traditional annealers hardware-expensive and slow for large instances like Max-Cut with thousands of nodes.
motivation: COPs are computationally demanding across many applications; existing Ising annealers suffer prohibitive hardware costs and iteration overhead due to dense matrix operations and transcendental function calculations.
method: A device-algorithm co-design using double-gate ferroelectric FET (DG FeFET) CiM crossbars with a novel incremental-E transformation that reduces VMV complexity from O(n²) to O(n) by computing energy changes incrementally; approximates exponential annealing with simplified fractional forms to enable efficient in-situ computation within a tunable back-gate annealing flow.
key_novelty: Incremental-E transformation reducing Ising energy computation from O(n²) to O(n) combined with ferroelectric CiM substrate for native in-situ annealing.
contributions: Novel incremental-E transformation reducing computational complexity from O(n²) to O(n)
DG FeFET-based CiM crossbar architecture for efficient in-situ energy computation
Simplified fractional approximation of exponential annealing factors
1503-1716× energy reduction and 8.08-8.15× speedup on 3000-node Max-Cut vs. prior annealers
limitations: Evaluation limited to Max-Cut; scalability to other COP types and real hardware fabrication timelines not discussed.
primary_theme: ferroelectric CiM accelerator for efficient combinatorial optimization via complexity reduction
